title: 5.4.3 Sub-build: Score once
description: One ball, one bumper, one score. Build the smallest thing that scores once per hit, before you put the same idea into your table.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: The ball falls onto the bumper and bounces away. The score stays at 0. Nothing here is a game yet: it is one sprite, one bumper and a number.

steps.title: Remember the frame before
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, store this frame's answer in a variable: `const touching = ball.colliding(bumper) > 0;`. Then keep the previous answer in a second variable that starts `false`, and add 1 to the score only when `touching` is true and the remembered one is false. At the end of `draw()`, give the memory this frame's answer.
hints: `colliding()` answers with a number: 0 apart, more than 0 while touching. Comparing with `> 0` turns it into true or false.
If the score climbs every frame, the score line is outside the `if`, or the memory is never updated.

steps.title: Prove it is once
steps.instructions: Run it. The ball lands, bounces, lands again: the score should go up by 1 per landing, not 60 per second. Change the ball's `y` in `setup()` and watch it count again.

requirements.title: This frame is stored
requirements.description: A variable holds this frame's collision answer (const/let/var = ... colliding(...) or overlaps(...)), so the same answer is used twice. Help: 5.4.1 (Reading: A collision is not an event)

requirements.title: Score changes on the edge
requirements.description: The score is added to inside an `if` that tests the stored answer and the frame before (`if (touching && !wasTouching)` or equivalent). Help: 5.4.1 (Reading: A collision is not an event)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Score once". The task: store this frame's collision answer in a variable, remember the previous frame in another variable that starts false, add 1 to the score only when the answer is true and the memory is false, and update the memory every frame. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic, so judge the mechanic itself and not style. Accept any variable names, helper functions, arrow functions, ternaries and semicolons. A line that only exists in a comment or a string does not count. moSHion facts: colliding(b) is 0 while apart and counts frames while touching, so an if on it alone is true every frame of a touch; a stored "last frame" value makes it true once. .life = n counts down one per frame and deletes the sprite at 0. A sprite with collider 'none' is passed through and has its gravity off. loadSound(name) in setup() (a built-in name such as 'coin', or a full path such as '/moshion/assets/coin.wav') and sound.play() where the event happens; a browser will not play sound before the student's first click or key. Write short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name the student's own line when something is missing, and never write corrected code.

rubric.title: The answer is stored
rubric.description: This frame's collision answer is in a variable (colliding() > 0, overlaps(), or a comparison), not asked twice.

rubric.title: The score fires on the edge only
rubric.description: Adding to the score happens under an if that tests the stored answer AND the memory being false, so a held touch counts once.
